# Draft:Kumbha's conquest of Marwar

Kumbha's conquest of Marwar was a significant military campaign conducted by Maharana Kumbha of Mewar against his fellow Rathore Rajputs of the Kingdom of Marwar. It was the culmination of events that had taken place from the marriage of the princes of Marwar Hansabai to the Maharana of Mewar Lakha.  The ruler of Marwar Rao Ranmal Rathore who had designs on Mewar was assassinated in Mewar only which took Marwar by surprise and as a result, Marwar was captured in a swift military campaign by Chunda, one of the nobles and earlier heir apparent to the throne of Mewar.
Prelude
In the last few years of Rana Lakha's reign. Crown prince of Marwar Ranmal came to Mewar seeking asylum and support to regain the throne which was rightfully his as he was banished by his father. To strengthen his claim, Prince Ranmal proposed a marriage alliance between the two kingdoms, which was intended to secure Mewar's support for his efforts. The proposal was presented in front of Maharana Lakha for crown price Chunda. However, due to some misunderstanding Chunda said that Hansabai would marry his father Lakha not him. Upon which, Ranmal put an condition that only the son from Hansabai and Lakha would become the King on which Chunda agreed and abdicated the throne. With the assistance of Mewar's military forces, Ranmal successfully regained the throne of Marwar and established himself as a vassal ally of Mewar.
Following Ranmal's ascension, Rana Lakha passed away, and Chunda became the regent of Mokal, the son from Hansabai and Lakha's marriage. However afraid of increasing influence of Chunda. He was ordered to leave Mewar and Hansabai requested that Ranmal to assist in governing on behalf of her son, Mokal, which he did with unwavering loyalty. However, Mewar faced significant challenges once more when Mokal was assassinated in a coup d'état. In response to this turmoil, Hansabai again called upon Ranmal to manage the ensuing rebellion, and he effectively restored order on behalf of her grandson, Kumbha.
Regrettably, as time progressed, Ranmal began to demonstrate a desire for greater power, leading to a conflict with Raghadeva, a prominent noble within the court. This dispute ultimately culminated in Raghadeva's death, which occurred as a result of Ranmal employing a poisoned robe. Furthermore, in an effort to consolidate his influence, Ranmal appointed several of his own relatives to key positions within the administration, which significantly escalated tensions in the region. One day, Ranmal was waiting for one of the mistress he loved. In doing so, he felt bit agitated as she took time on being asked she said that "I would come only when those I serve would allow me" on which Ranmal replied that in few days "he would be his master". The maid became suspicious of Ranmal and reported this matter to queen mother Hansabai and Kumbha in which it was decided that Ranmal has to be dealt with brute force only. Chunda was called back which also put Ranmal to alarm and he ordered his sons particulary the Jodha to live in Talhati(lower citadel).
Conquest of Marwar
One fine day when Ranmal was heavily drunk and was unconscious. Taking advantage of the situation Ranmal hands were tied to the bed and he was put to death by several assassins. This news spread like wildfire and Jodha rushed from the lower citadel to Marwar being chased by Chunda and Mewari soldiers. There were many melee fights  between Rathores and Sisodiyas, in which Jodha lost 200 of his own but killed 400 of the enemy. Some important chiefs of Marwar lost their lives in the process and their names were
* Chandrawat
* Shivaraj
* Puna Bhati
* Bhima
* Barishal
* Bajrang Bhimawat
* Bhim(Ranma l's brother)
Jodha reached Mandal where his brother Kandhal too joined him and they both started for Mandore(the capital of Marwar). He soon reached Someshwara pass, a small mountain defile which divided Mewar and Marwar with only 100 horsemen. Choonda soon tracked them paving the way for another hand-to-hand combat which resulted in only 7 narrowly escaping from being captured. Jodha soon reached Mandore. Choonda on the other hand wasted no time to allow Rathores to summon their bannerman and besieged Mandore. After days of continuous fighting Mandore fell to Mewari forces and Jodha was forced to leave the place being also chased by attackers. He soon reached Sojat which also got captured in a few days so were the other important towns of Marwar.
Maharana Kumbha did not follow the policy of the complete annihilation of Rathores which in all circumstances was impossible. Instead, he won over the sections of Rathores. Sojat was granted to Raghavadeva and Narbad another brother of Ranmal who was an assistant of Kumbha. In this way, Kumbha gave most of Marwar to the samants(feudal chiefs) of the Rathore branch only and only Mandor was retained by Kumbha.
